1a8de85b424cf0c31382dac7c65f167ef71b8457: Gryon offers 87 km of well-marked runs — a mid-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 30 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Gryon's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for learning to ski with children. Gryon's altitude (1130 m at the bottom, 2120 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Gryon is clearly on the expensive side: €73 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the priciest in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but be aware of it before you go. In short: Gryon keeps its promises. A resort in the Northern Alps that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
1aab92ae8aca88f16f3b09cb86a45078dfeb0ad1: The Courchevel ski area, with its 150 km of runs, offers a fine choice for every type of skier: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 39 lifts let you link runs without long queues. Courchevel's DNA is high-end: the accommodation, the mountain restaurants and the resort services reflect a clientele that doesn't count the cost. At 77€ for a day lift pass, the stay comes at a price, but the experience lives up to it for anyone who wants to indulge without compromise. With a summit at 2738 m and a village at 1850 m, Courchevel's snow reliability is generally good from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause strains early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfall arrives. The budget for a stay in Courchevel is clearly high: 77€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Courchevel isn't for everyone, but for those who can afford it, it's probably one of the best skiing experiences in Europe.
